ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the square $ABCD$, point $F$ is on the side $CD$, and $BF$ intersects $AC$ at point $E$. If $\angle CBF=20^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle AED$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ quadrilateral ABCD is a square\\
$\therefore \angle ACB = \angle ACD = \angle BAC = \angle CAD = 45^\circ$, $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$, AB = AD\\
$\because \angle FBC = 20^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle ABF = 70^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ in $\triangle ABE$, $\angle AEB = 65^\circ$\\
In $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle ADE$\\
$ \left\{\begin{array}{l}
AB = AD \\
\angle BAE = \angle EAD = 45^\circ \\
AE = AE
\end{array}\right.$ \\
$\therefore \triangle ABE \cong \triangle ADE$\\
$\therefore \angle AED = \angle AEB = \boxed{65^\circ}$

The diagonal AC has equation y = 1 − x, while BF has equation y = x tan 20°. Their intersection E satisfies x = 1/(1 + tan 20°), y = tan 20°/(1 + tan 20°). Now compute directions of the rays from E: EA points along diagonal AC toward A, direction 135° from the positive x-axis; ED has vector D − E = (tan20°/(1+tan20°), 1/(1+tan20°)), whose direction is arctan(cot20°) = 70°. ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ quadrilateral ABCD is a square\\
$\therefore \angle ACB = \angle ACD = \angle BAC = \angle CAD = 45^\circ$, $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$, AB = AD\\
$\because \angle FBC = 20^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle ABF = 70^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ in $\triangle ABE$, $\angle AEB = 65^\circ$\\
In $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle ADE$\\
$ \left\{\begin{array}{l}
AB = AD \\
\angle BAE = \angle EAD = 45^\circ \\
AE = AE
\end{array}\right.$ \\
$\therefore \triangle ABE \cong \triangle ADE$\\
$\therefore \angle AED = \angle AEB = \boxed{65^\circ}$

Image description: In the figure is square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point F is on the right side CD, segment BF intersects diagonal AC at E, and ED is also connected in the figure. The marked condition is ∠CBF = 20°.

Reasoning: Because ABCD is a square, AB ⟂ BC, and ∠ABC = 90°. It is known that ∠CBF = 20°, and BF is inside ∠ABC, therefore ∠ABF = 90° - 20° = 70°. Also because AC is a diagonal of the square, AC forms 45° with AB, that is, in triangle ABE, ∠BAE = 45°. Therefore ∠AEB = 180° - 70° - 45° = 65°. The square is symmetric about diagonal AC, B's symmetric point with respect to AC is D, while A and E both remain fixed on AC, so ray EB is symmetric to ED, and ray EA remains unchanged; hence ∠AED = ∠AEB = 65°.
